========================================
## Create tarball of UEMCloud

# install jdk17
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y openjdk-17-jdk-headless

# install mvn
wget http://enterprise-nexus.rim.net/nexus/content/repositories/ebu-thirdparty/apache/maven/3.6.3/maven-3.6.3-bin.tar.gz
tar xzf maven-3.6.3-bin.tar.gz

# install BB RSA root certificate
echo  | base64 -d | gzip -d | sudo tee BB_rsa.crt
sudo update-ca-certificates

# configure maven (quoted base64; gzip -dc; segment must be Li0VfOybBafYQ4 not Li0VfOyBBafYQ4 -- BB vs bB typo breaks gzip CRC)
mkdir -p ~/.m2
echo '' | base64 -d | gzip -dc | sed -e "s|/opt/uemcloud|${HOME}|g" > ~/.m2/settings.xml

# build -- change the version to that which you want to build
mkdir -p build/43.32
cd build/43.32
wget http://enterprise-nexus.rim.net/nexus/content/repositories/ebu-releases/com/blackberry/enterprise/uem.catalog/43.32.0/uem.catalog-43.32.0-cloud.xml -O cloud.xml
~/apache-maven-3.6.3/bin/mvn clean install -Dbundle -B -f cloud.xml -DbundleVersion=43-32-0

========================================
## Using the tarball

kfong@CI0600000002993:~/build/43.32/target$ find bundle -type f | sort
bundle/artifacts/uos_build/uem.catalog.cloud-43.32.0.tar   # this is the package that includes the Database manager, and the Core/UI pairing
bundle/env/common/default_cloud_product.yml
bundle/env/common/default_fedramp_product.yml
bundle/env/common/uos-machine.properties
bundle/env/common/uos-partition.properties

# Assuming that you copied over the tarball to a fresh host

# Extract tarball and properties file to host
tar xvf ~/uem.catalog.cloud-43.32.0.tar

# Run DB manager to setup/upgrade schema
cd ~/DatabaseLinux/context
cp ~/partition.properties . # assuming that you have the contextualized file in ~
./start.sh

# Something to do with snapins
cd ~/CoreUILinux
java -cp pods/*:tools/lib/* com.rim.mdm.config.tools.pod.PodDeployer --instructorFile pods/cloud/bes12pods.instructor --propertiesFile ~/machine.properties

# Application Start
cd ~/CoreUILinux/context
cp ~/machine.properties .
./context.sh
./start.sh

========================================
Contextualization
CDK has a mechanism to replace the %{} variables in the properties file with variables set in a number of YML files.
During the prototyping, I would do these by hand to know what is being replaced, and possibly figuring out what properties are not needed.
For long term, I would suggest converting the file, replacing all %{} with {{ }} and using Jinja2 templating.

I would advise AGAINST using CDK for anything -- it's purpose built for deploying very specific things in Lab90 and Azure in very specific ways.

========================================
PostgreSQL Cluster
In Lab90, clusters are built and configured using Terraform and Ansible -- this part is extractable out of CDK and will be provided on the side, nothing much changes.
In the long term, I would suggest adapting the automation to fit the service that you want to deploy.
Managing the PostgreSQL cluster is outside the scope of this -- if there is a need for training/guidance, I would request help from the former DBAs.

[enterprise-gerrit.rim.net:29418/enterprise/cdk/cdk-tools.git :: enterprise.deployment.cdk-cloud-configs/src/configs/lab90/postgres]


========================================
Configuration
The out of the box configuration of UEMCloud will not work as an equivalent OnPrem version.

There are configs that turn UEM into the Cloud SaaS solution, and configs that are turned off because it's not OnPrem.
These configurations will need to be provided by Development -- GTS does not expertise in deploying OnPrem, and does not know how the switches work.
The configuration files that are provided to us are specifically for UEMCloud.

There are some private keys/certificates/configurations that are owned and managed by BlackBerry that *should not* be given to the customer *under any circumstances*.
For any of these, there should be equivalent functionality in OnPrem where the customer is able to get their own, *OR* it's SaaS only and not required by the customer.

========================================
Other Considerations

1/ Observability
GTS uses self-hosted Grafana products for visualization, deployed in AWS.

The monitoring stack consists of a Cortex/Mimir backend for storage, with Prometheus performing polling against agents on the hosts.
The logging stack consist of Loki backend for storage, with fluent-bit used to send logs from host.

It is unlikely that we will want to host customer logs/monitoring.
I suspect that each customer will want some control over their data, and integrate it into their own solution, so all this will likely be bespoke.
